expr: (list (with-temp-buffer (insert "abcdef") (goto-char (point-min)) (list (re-search-forward "z" nil (quote move)) (point))) (with-temp-buffer (insert "abcdef") (goto-char (point-min)) (list (search-forward "z" 3 (quote move)) (point))) (with-temp-buffer (insert "abcdef") (goto-char (point-max)) (list (re-search-backward "z" nil (quote move)) (point))) (with-temp-buffer (insert "abcdef") (goto-char (point-max)) (list (search-backward "z" 3 (quote move)) (point))))
note: THE THIRD ANSWER, the one a two-valued reading of NOERROR misses entirely. Emacs answers ((nil 7) (nil 3) (nil 1) (nil 3)): any non-nil, non-t NOERROR returns nil AND MOVES POINT TO THE LIMIT -- to BOUND when one was given, and to point-max (forward) or point-min (backward) when BOUND is nil. All four combinations are here because the limit differs by direction and a binding that moved to point-max in both would pass the two forward cases. kg answers `wrong-number-of-arguments'. THE DECISION, MADE: kg implements all three answers for all four names; the third is not optional, because `t' and `'move' differ only in where point ends up and a caller that wanted the move has no other way to ask.
